name: The hook
text: Your tooth hurts. It is fourteen thousand years ago. There is no dental clinic down the road. So did people simply do nothing?

name: An archaeological clue
text: Not always. At Villabruna, in northern Italy, researchers studied a human molar with a cavity. Inside it, they found tiny scratches and chipped enamel.

name: What the marks suggest
text: Experiments suggested that pointed flint tools had scraped the cavity while the person was alive. Think careful scraping, not a modern dentist's drill.

name: What we do not know
text: That is evidence of an attempt to treat a damaged tooth. It does not tell us exactly how it felt, who helped, or whether the treatment worked.

name: The punchline
text: The person holding their cheek here is imaginary. The ancient tooth is real. Our ancestors had serious skills. I would still rather book an appointment.
